conviction_note: Fabege does not guide, so the release carries no guidance event. The period was not pre-released, but 13 analysts cover the name and on six of its last eight reports the stock moved under 1%, including the Q2 2026 beat of 8% on property-management result, which closed +0.8%. Several small sourced positives point the same way: one broker at about +5% to consensus, a flat policy rate, stable Q3 Stockholm valuations at the closest peer, positive net lettings already known, and an unused 10% buyback mandate with the shares at about 45% of NRV. They lean p_up only to 55 on an abs_move of 2.5, so the scaled number is +0.25 against a findings sum of +0.85. The gap is the reaction history (beats here are not bought) plus heavy coverage.

findings.finding: Arctic Securities says its Q3 profit-from-property-management forecast is about 5% above consensus. It kept a buy rating and cut its target to SEK 80 on rate sensitivity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 management result 403 vs Bloomberg consensus 372 (+8%), and the stock closed +0.8% on the day, then -4.4% two sessions later. Q3 2025: 393 vs 382 (+2.9%) with positive net letting, +9.3% on the day. Q3 2024: miss of 4.7%, -3.2%.
findings.original_quote: Inför rapporten för tredje kvartalet ligger resultatprognosen omkring 5 procent över konsensus. (Ahead of the Q3 report, the earnings forecast is about 5 percent above consensus.)
findings.why_not_priced: This is one broker's forecast, not a company number, and the same note cut 2027-28 estimates by 10%; the market has traded the forward cut, not the Q3 beat. If the beat were priced, the stock would not be at the 52-week low with a 20-day run-up of -5.5%. Partly priced at best, because the note is public wire copy.
findings.independence: Q2 run-rate from the company's own report: Q2 management result 403 against a Q3 2025 base of 393 (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b647a74e8ff8d3633768317f8c34efcfe&lang=en&src=listed)

findings.finding: Q3 net lettings will include the DNB lease signed 20 July, a net letting effect of about +SEK 66m, so the quarter flips positive after Q2's -86m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 net letting of +9m came with 'tecken på ljusning' (signs of improvement) from the CEO, and the stock rose 9.3%. Q2 2026 net letting of -86m came with a beat, and the stock was flat to down.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a public MAR release from three months ago, and the stock fell 12% after it. Only the rest of Q3 net lettings is new. Sized near 0 under the already-public rule.
findings.independence: Swedish release of the same deal (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=ba7a8d026fa2e26c689b13f3e22413f16&lang=sv&src=listed); same fact, not independent

findings.finding: Atrium Ljungberg, the closest Stockholm office peer, reported on 9 Oct that its Q3 average yield requirement was unchanged, with slightly lower yields for some inner-city assets and rents still rising in Hagastaden, where Fabege has Haga Norra. Fabege's Q3 value changes are therefore more likely near zero or positive than a rate-driven write-down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 value changes were +120m (the first positive quarter), and the stock was +0.8% on the day. Q3 2025 value changes were -338m, offset by tone, and the stock was +9.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Fabege has fallen about 17% since 7 July (78.80 to 65.40), against -6% to -12% for Castellum, Wallenstam and Hufvudstaden, on the market's fear that rising rates hit its low-yielding portfolio. If valuers had not moved in Q3, a write-down would not be what the price is braced for. Transmission from a peer: a proxy, and Atrium Ljungberg's own stock fell 4.5% on its report.
findings.independence: Fabege's own Q2 report: average yield requirement 4.57% (4.59%), value changes positive in Q2 (https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/ae6834cc677493e65cb650d6d81dbc28a)

findings.finding: The Riksbank held its policy rate at 1.75% through Q3 (unchanged since September 2025, held again on 24 September 2026). With 53% of Fabege's debt at floating rates and an average rate of 2.88% at 30 June, Q3 net interest should sit near Q2's -252m. The rate selloff is a forward risk and not yet in the Q3 numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net interest has not been a surprise line; Q2 net interest of -252m vs -240m did not move the stock.
findings.original_quote: Riksbanken lämnar styrräntan oförändrad på 1,75 procent (search-snippet rendering of the decision; page not fetched)
findings.why_not_priced: The decision is public and in every model, so this is mostly priced. What it does is limit how far the Q3 numbers can show the rate damage that Arctic's -10% 2027-28 cut assumes; the market's de-rating rests on forward rates.
findings.independence: Atrium Ljungberg Q3: 'No effect is visible on our average interest rate yet' (https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a2abca193edae7b3e8d48c8a8a02e8948)

findings.finding: Fabege has an AGM mandate, valid to the 2027 AGM, to buy back up to 10% of its shares. The stock trades at about 45% of its last EPRA NRV (SEK 65.4 against 144), and Arctic says publicly that buybacks are needed to justify its target. A buyback announcement with the report is possible but has no company signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no observed buyback announcement in the sampled report history; the 16.2m treasury shares cancelled in June 2026 came from earlier buybacks
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected buybacks, the discount to NRV would not have widened through a 17% fall. An announcement would be new on the day. Low probability: LTV is 43% and the CEO's priority is 'protect cash flow, balance sheet strength', so this is sized as a small expectation with a wide upper tail.
findings.independence: Arctic note calling for buybacks: 'Arctic Securities anser att aktieåterköp krävs för att motivera den nya riktkursen' (https://www.placera.se/telegram/fabege-arctic-securities-sanker-riktkursen-for-fabege-till-80-kronor-hoppas-pa-aterkop-20261012)

findings.finding: The remaining Haga Norra tenant-owned phases were only 40% (Mathilda, completion Q2-Q3 2026) and 47% (Ingetora, Q3-Q4 2026) sold at 30 June. Q3 residential settlements, which are revenue-recognised on completion, may therefore come in below the 39m gross profit residential development contributed in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Residential development drove the Q2 beat (gross profit 39m vs 29m); no isolated reaction history on this line
findings.why_not_priced: The selling grades are in the Q2 report's project table, and most analysts model settlements from it, so this is largely priced. It is the one line where the Q3 management result could fall short of a run-rate extrapolated from Q2.

findings.finding: Consensus has Q3 rental income at SEK 894m, BELOW Q2's 902m, although rental income rose sequentially from Q2 to Q3 last year (852 to 864) and completed projects added about SEK 100m to H1 income. The bar looks low unless Q2 move-outs bite harder than the company indicated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rental income has printed within ±0.3% of consensus for the last three quarters (Q3 2025 864 vs 865; Q1 2026 in line; Q2 2026 902 vs 899), with no reaction on this line.
findings.original_quote: Hyresintäkter 894 13 864 (rental income consensus 894, 13 estimates, 864 last year)
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from the shape of consensus. Thirteen analysts know about the Q2 move-outs (City, Arenastaden) that the CEO letter cites, and those probably explain the step down. Rental income has hugged consensus for three quarters, so a material beat is unlikely; sized small.

outside_window.finding: Telenor terminates its Solna lease, moving out in Q3 2028; DNB Sweden takes over Max Matthiessen's premises in Q1 2027. Both are rental-income effects years after the window.
Riksbank next policy decision on 4 Nov 2026. Forward rate risk is the market's main concern for Fabege, which has a 1.4-year fixed-rate period.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the priced lean (+1.84, from shorts covering 2.21 to 2.04 and the -12.8% 60-day mean-reversion term) and lean slightly against the falling 20- and 60-day run-up. Since they agree with positioning, part of what they say is already in the lean.
language_note: The Arctic Securities quantified preview (Q3 forecast ~5% above consensus, call for buybacks) appeared only in Swedish Finwire copy on placera.se.
The Modular Finance consensus (13 analysts, rental income 894 / NOI 689) and the last eight report-day reactions are from Swedish Börsvärlden/Finwire copy; no English source carried them.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': DNB net-letting finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1, Riksbank finding from +0.2 to +0.1.
'The move is in the guide' (none or reiterated: median 2.3%): Fabege gives no forecast, so abs_move_pct cut from 3.0 to 2.5.

'Coverage tells you which regime': 13 analysts and public wire copy, so the Arctic finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.3 and p_up from 56 to 55, because this name's beats have not been bought (Q2 +8% beat, +0.8%).
'A narrow proxy loses': peer read-through cut from +0.3 to +0.2, buyback inference from +0.3 to +0.2, rental-bar inference from +0.2 to +0.15.
